order: Execution Order 30 Sept 2026, items B4 (news, primary sources first) and E3 (congressional and executive trades)
written_by: scripts/fetch_news.py reads this registry; the list is frozen — a source is added or changed only by order
rule: primary sources first: Tier 1 = the issuer's own release (Fed, BEA, BLS, Census, DOL, SEC EDGAR filings, company investor relations); Tier 2 = secondary headline feeds, labeled; bodies never stored; summaries system-written
rule_source: the newsroom's founding principle (La Linterna, architecture of primary sources, February 2026): every story is generated from primary sources — official data, public records, government documents, direct statements of the actors, raw economic data; traditional media are an internal reference layer, seen but never cited or rewritten, stored as headlines only. Applied here as Tier 1 = the issuer's own release; Tier 2 = secondary headlines, shown but labeled

order_text.B4: News, primary sources first. Two tiers, stored as headline, source, URL, timestamp, tickers, and a system-written one-line summary; article bodies are never stored. Tier 1, primary: Federal Reserve press releases and speeches feed; BLS and BEA release pages on release days; SEC EDGAR filings feeds (8-K, 10-Q, 10-K, Form 4) for every held name and the top-40 board; company investor-relations press releases for held names. Tier 2, secondary and labeled as such: per-ticker headline feeds for held names. Relevance filter: held names, the board's top 40, and macro topics mapped to calendar event types. The news panel on the home page shows the last 24 hours, Tier 1 first; each held name's card shows its last five items.
order_text.E3: Congressional and executive trades: not added as signals, scores, or panels. If a disclosed trade in a held name appears in the Tier 2 news feed it is shown there as news, labeled with its disclosure lag, and nowhere else.

never_stored: the feed's own description / summary / content text

language_rules.vocabulary: the referee's two prohibited words (scripts/audit_nightly.py, language check) never appear in a stored item; the check runs on the full serialized item and again on the whole file before it is written; violating items are counted under excluded.vocabulary_rule, not stored
language_rules.directive: no stored text carries a buy/sell directive — the referee's tokens plus the plain-English imperative forms listed as DIRECTIVE_PATTERNS in scripts/fetch_news.py; violating items are counted under excluded.directive_rule, not stored
language_rules.trade_recommendation: nothing in the feed recommends a trade; a disclosed congressional or executive trade is news with its disclosure lag labeled, never a signal

relevance.top40: data/screen/scores.json watchlist rows with on_board_as == top40
relevance.macro: topic keywords in the title mapped to calendar event types (topic_keywords); Federal Reserve items are kept regardless of topic, other macro items only with a topic
relevance.tier2: a secondary headline is relevant only when it names a universe member (symbol as a whole word or a company-name phrase); the tickers stored are the members named

disclosure_lag_label: disclosed trade — reports lag the trade by up to 45 days; shown as news only, no signal

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board press release
sources.provenance: issuer feed, RSS 2.0 (title, link, category, pubDate); verified 200 on 2026-09-30; every Fed press release is Tier 1 relevant

sources.label: Federal Reserve speech
sources.provenance: issuer feed, RSS 2.0; verified 200 on 2026-09-30; the description (venue line) is not stored

sources.label: BEA release
sources.provenance: issuer feed, RSS 2.0 with one item per release back to 2013; verified 200 on 2026-09-30; the description carries release text and is never stored; NextReleaseDate (structured) is used in the summary; kept only with a topic (PCE, GDP, TRADE)

sources.label: BEA (release page)
sources.provenance: fallback used only when the BEA feed fails: release-day items constructed from data/event_calendar.json event types GDP and PCE (none registered in the calendar as of 2026-09-30) and the release schedule; nothing fetched

sources.label: BLS (release page)
sources.provenance: https://www.bls.gov/feed/bls_latest.rss returns 403 to automated clients (checked 2026-09-30), as do the release pages; on a release day (data/event_calendar.json, types CPI, NFP, PPI, JOLTS) a Tier 1 item is constructed from the schedule once the scheduled time has passed — headline 'BLS release: {release} ({reference month})', the live release-page URL with the release date as fragment, summary 'scheduled release at {time} ET; print not fetched'; nothing is fetched

sources.label: Census Bureau economic indicator
sources.provenance: issuer feed, RSS 2.0 (one item per indicator, link = indicator page); verified 200 on 2026-09-30; kept only with a topic — retail sales (RETAIL) and international trade (TRADE) release days

sources.label: Department of Labor release
sources.provenance: issuer feed, RSS 2.0 (2-digit-year pubDate); verified 200 on 2026-09-30; kept only with a topic — weekly claims (CLAIMS)

sources.label: SEC EDGAR filing
sources.universe: held names and the top-40 board
sources.provenance: issuer record (filings.recent: accessionNumber, filingDate, acceptanceDateTime, form, primaryDocument, primaryDocDescription); every EDGAR endpoint returns 403 unless the User-Agent declares a contact in the SEC's required form, read from the environment variable SEC_USER_AGENT (never hardcoded) — unset means the source is skipped and recorded as such; headline '{form} filed by {company}' (Form 4 spelled out), no body parsing; summary 'EDGAR {form} · filed {date} · {primaryDocDescription or form}'; timestamp = acceptanceDateTime, else noon ET of the filing date; sequential requests at most 8 per second

sources.label: Broadcom investor relations
sources.provenance: issuer press-release feed (Q4 platform), RSS 2.0; verified 200 on 2026-09-30

sources.label: NVIDIA investor relations
sources.provenance: issuer press-release feed found on the index page https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/rss (an HTML page listing feeds), category 'press_release'; verified 200 on 2026-09-30, 20 items, press releases only (/releases.xml and /rss.xml mix in blog posts and are not used)

sources.label: GE Vernova investor relations
sources.provenance: issuer press-release feed linked from https://www.gevernova.com/news/press-releases; verified 200 on 2026-09-30, 20 press releases (links under /news/press-releases/); the pubDate carries a line break before the zone, normalized at parse. Not used: /news/rss (404), /news/rss.xml (media-contact entries and feature articles), /rss.xml (investor events and leadership pages)

sources.label: Alphabet investor relations
sources.provenance: https://abc.xyz/investor/ has no RSS link and no alternate feed element; press releases for GOOG come through EDGAR 8-K filings (Tier 1) and the Tier 2 headline feed

sources.label: BitMine investor relations
sources.provenance: press releases are distributed through PR Newswire (https://bitminetech.io/investor-relations links them; the PR Newswire company page offers no organization feed); the GlobeNewswire keyword feed https://www.globenewswire.com/RssFeed/keyword/bitmine%20immersion/feedTitle/BitMine is stale (last item 2024-04-22) and is not used; filings come through EDGAR (Tier 1) and headlines through Tier 2

sources.label: Micron investor relations
sources.provenance: Q4-platform feed; returns 403 to the declared User-Agent; skipped until it answers; filings come through EDGAR (Tier 1) and headlines through Tier 2

sources.label: Arista investor relations
sources.provenance: Q4-platform feed; returns 403 to the declared User-Agent; skipped until it answers; filings come through EDGAR (Tier 1) and headlines through Tier 2

sources.label: Yahoo Finance headline feed (secondary)
sources.provenance: yfinance Ticker.news, verified 2026-09-30: content.title, content.pubDate (ISO Z), content.provider.displayName (stored as source), content.canonicalUrl.url or clickThroughUrl.url (stored as url); content.description and content.summary are never read; every item is labeled tier 2 / secondary; summary 'Tier 2 headline · {provider} · about {tickers}'; a headline is relevant only when it names a universe member
